transcript.text: Section 3. You will hear a conversation between a tutor and a student about a university course.

transcript.text: First, you have some time to read through questions 14 to 17.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Hi, I've come to ask a few questions about the literature degree you offer.

transcript.speaker: Joanna
transcript.text: Oh yes. Well, I'm a tutor for undergraduate literature students here at Southampton University. My name is Joanna. Could you give me your name?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: My name's Tom. Tom Atkins. I'm hoping to enroll in a literature program this coming term.

transcript.speaker: Joanna
transcript.text: Oh really? Are you working at the moment?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I am currently working part-time at a publishing company as an editing administrator for a monthly journal, but I work from home for only about 10 hours per week, so I have time to study.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: And I am particularly interested in the comparative literature course, especially the elements related to post-colonial literature. I studied that a bit in a previous literature class I took and I'm curious to learn more.

transcript.text: That's my field of study too. So are you interested in studying full-time?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yes, I am. And I'd like to know a bit more about the other requirements for the course, how long it will take, and what are the required courses and alternative courses?

transcript.speaker: Joanna
transcript.text: Of course. The degree takes three years to complete. In the first year, there are three modules you have to take, which are introductory courses in literature and literary theory, in addition to one optional module within the department.
transcript.highlight_text: In the first year, there are three modules you have to take, which are introductory courses

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: What are the subjects for the optional modules?

transcript.speaker: Joanna
transcript.text: They change every year, but past modules have been on topics like Indian literature, basically thematic courses.
transcript.highlight_text: past modules have been on topics like Indian literature

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: And I can only take one optional module?

transcript.speaker: Joanna
transcript.text: You won't have room in your schedule for any more during the first year, unfortunately. But in the second year, you have only one compulsory module and can take three optional ones. The second year's modules are much more specific and they will allow you to focus your studies before the dissertation the following year.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: And then in your third year, the modules will help determine the kind of research you do for your dissertation.
